hypothesis: A frozen structural cost selector can exploit complementary regenerative algorithms while numerical enclosure independently preserves the requested accuracy.
minimal_test: 24 calibration cases,48 predefined heldouts; both fixed baselines and selector; include validation/retries; exact model inputs, interval outputs and rational spot checks.

refutations.claim: A small absolute discrepancy guarantees useful relative precision on rare probabilities.
refutations.evidence: 2.22e-16 floating cancellation result vs2.4644e-31 rational probability; adaptive enclosures reject inadequate precision.

refutations.claim: Correctness depends on choosing the fastest algorithm correctly.
refutations.evidence: Even a deliberately wrong predictor returns only intervals meeting the same mathematical gate.

refutations.claim: Arithmetic-operation counts alone capture equivalent solver costs.
refutations.evidence: All precision-refinement passes and integer resolution costs are included; algebraic equivalence does not imply numerical interchangeability.

next_gate: Independent public-model coverage and matched-accuracy official comparison; no general SOTA claim from generated holdouts.
historical_policy: Additive record; no altered global counts or erased prior evidence. Validity, concrete contribution, priority and fertility are distinct.
